To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

individual differences accounted for a large proportion of the variance in people’s TRIM scores, but that these dispositions were not stable across situations, and that they were predicted by Neuroticism and by Agreeableness, but only for Neuroticism were the associations mediated by appraisal of transgression severity.
people’s transgression related motivations are moderately consistent across situations and are predicted by their levels of Neuroticism and/or Agreeableness.

people’s TRIM dispositions are moderately stable across time and situations but that they are also influenced by the specific nature of transgressions, the specific nature of the relationship with the transgressor, and the context in which the transgression occurs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the personality correlates of transgression-related motivational tendencies.
the personality bases of people’s responses to transgressions and with the generalizability of those responses.
individual differences in transgression-related motivational tendencies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Big Five personality factors are not a sufficient basis for understanding the TRIMs, but that they may be a necessary basis for doing so.
individual differences in people’s transgression related motivational dispositions can be reliably measured with a single transgression scenario.

transgression-related interpersonal motives (TRIM) are not only influenced by the personality trait neuroticism, but that the influence of neuroticism is mediated by appraisement of transgression severity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people who are high on Neuroticism and low on Agreeableness are more likely to respond to a transgression with avoidance, benevolences, or revenge.

the TRIMs have personality correlates, but that these correlates are not consistent enough across situations to permit the estimation of individual differences in TRIMs on the basis of responses to a single situation.
individual differences are important for understanding transgression-related motivational processes, but they are not as important as transgression severity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TRIM model is a useful way to understand people’s responses to transgressions.

the Big Five personality factors are important predictors of people’s transgression- related motivational dispositions, which in turn are important predictors of how they will react to specific transgressions.
the TRIMs are moderately to highly stable, and they can be predicted from people’s Big Five personality traits.
